conventions.convention: The no-arrow A1 moment equation is IJ=0; positive stability means J is injective. Framed inclusions use the identity on W, I=ξI′ and J′=Jξ.
Hall modules are unital R-algebra representations into End_R(M), whose multiplication is composition. The zero module is allowed; tensor-product actions require additional structure.

The generic parameter is an indeterminate t and the Fock coefficient field is Q(t). The exact Hall map sends u_(1^r) to t^(-r(r-1)/2)e_r. Transported Green norms are δ_λμ z_λ ∏(t^(λ_i)−1)^(-1), distinct from ordinary Hall norms.

The arbitrary-framing geometry assumes AC, uses W=C^w with w≥0 and 0≤v≤w, and identifies M_v with T*Gr(v,W). The common-endomorphism Hecke model is the conormal correspondence after negating the second cotangent factor.

Intersection and convolution use rational Chow groups with support retained on the indicated fiber products and zero fibers; classes are not identified through possibly noninjective pushforward to the ambient cotangent bundles.

F uses the forward Hecke cycle, E uses the reversed cycle multiplied by (−1)^(a_v−a_(v+1))=(−1)^(w−1), and H has weight w−2v. Nonexistent endpoint terms are zero. The representation concerns ordinary top zero-fiber Chow groups.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC, the stable algebraic orbit space is M_v=T*Gr(v,W), with projective common-endomorphism map and zero fiber the zero section. Z_v=Tot Hom(W/T,S) is the signed conormal Hecke correspondence, has dimension a_v+a_(v+1), has projective projections, and meets either zero-section inverse image scheme-theoretically in Y_v.

Supported refined-diagonal convolution is associative, diagonal fundamental classes are units, and D⋆(C⋆α)=(D⋆C)⋆α. All indicated pushforwards are proper on their supports; a cycle of degree a_u+a_v acts between top zero-fiber Chow groups.
The forward supported zero-section intersection and pushforward is (−1)^v(v+1)[X_(v+1)]; the reverse calculation is (−1)^(w−v−1)(w−v)[X_v], in ordinary rational top Chow groups.
An R-linear representation of a unital associative R-algebra H on M is a unital R-algebra homomorphism ρ:H→End_R(M); when H is a Hall algebra, this is a Hall-algebra module.

On the generic Jordan Hall regular module transported to Q(t)[p_1,p_2,…], multiplication X_n by p_n has Green adjoint X_n†p_λ=n m_n(λ)/(t^n−1) p_(λ\(n)). Its normalization P_n=(t^n−1)X_n†/n is ∂/∂p_n. For each finite N these operators, with Z acting as identity, represent the finite Heisenberg Lie algebra, with vacuum 1.
For the specified framing-one data, M(0,1), M(1,1), M_0(0,1), M_0(1,1), L(0,1), L(1,1) and P_(0,1) are single points; the correspondence projections are identity maps of points.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite is reading context. The consumer explicitly separates Euler-twisted coproduct conventions from its untwisted module and Jordan transported pairing; it imports no general Green compatibility or Ringel theorem.
The Fock theorem uses the actual finite Heisenberg definition and bracket lemma: [P_i,X_j]=δ_ij Z, with Z acting as identity. Its polynomial representation asserts no analytic exponentiation.

The downstream page treats preceding constructions as reading context. Its interpretation remark faithfully describes a Hall module as an algebra action on a separate module and imports no Fock, geometric-action or physical state-counting conclusion.
